### Candidate 1: Feminist Structure Signal
*   **Exact Title:** Forging Ahead: Recent Acquisitions of Black Women Artists
*   **Source URL:** [https://www.nypl.org/news/press-release/2026/08/27/schomburg-centers-newest-exhibition-features-its-largest-show-contemporary-black-womens-art](https://www.nypl.org/news/press-release/2026/08/27/schomburg-centers-newest-exhibition-features-its-largest-show-contemporary-black-womens-art)
*   **Publication Date:** Press Release August 27, 2026 (Exhibition opened on September 24, 2026, and runs through March 27, 2027)
*   **Proposed Section:** Feminist Structure Signal
*   **Duplication Assessment:** **New Signal** (No previous mention of this exhibition or the Schomburg Center's acquisitions in the recent-issue context).
*   **Verified Facts:**
    *   **What Happened:** The Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture (a research division of the New York Public Library) has opened its largest-ever contemporary exhibition dedicated to recent acquisitions of Black women artists. 
    *   **Curators:** Curated by La Tanya S. Autry (Associate Curator, Photographs and Prints) and Tammi Lawson (Curator, Art and Artifacts).
    *   **Scope & Artists:** The exhibition features paintings, textiles, collages, sculpture, and photography from 21 contemporary Black women artists. Featured artists include Simone Leigh, Nona Faustine, Tschabalala Self, Xenobia Bailey, Helina Metaferia, and Firelei Baez. 
    *   **Acquisition Highlights:** Key acquisitions purchased specifically in honor of the Schomburg Center's 100th anniversary include a porcelain bust (*Untitled*, 2023) by Simone Leigh, and conceptual photographer Nona Faustine's *Mitochondria* series and selections from her *White Shoes* series.
*   **Relevance to Muki:** 
    This project is a concrete example of institutional counter-archiving. It directly addresses the historical gender disparities in archives and collections. Muki should track how the curators use acquisition policies to actively dismantle historical erasures, especially through photography and bodily iconography.

### Candidate 2: Visual Culture Signal
*   **Exact Title:** Ana Mendieta at Tate Modern
*   **Source URL:** [https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on/tate-modern/ana-mendieta](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on/tate-modern/ana-mendieta)
*   **Publication/Exhibition Dates:** July 14, 2026 – January 17, 2027 (Active events in September 2026)
*   **Proposed Section:** Visual Culture Signal
*   **Duplication Assessment:** **New Signal** (Mendieta's retrospective has not been covered in the recent 7-issue context).
*   **Verified Facts:**
    *   **What Happened:** Tate Modern is hosting the first major UK retrospective of Cuban-American artist Ana Mendieta (1948–1985) in over a decade. 
    *   **Scope:** Features over 120 works spanning sculpture, photography, drawings, and newly remastered films. It covers her iconic *Silueta Series* (earth-body works recorded via photography and film), early paintings, and late sculptural works.
    *   **Context/Recent Events:** On September 25, 2026, the museum hosted "Tate Modern Lates" focused entirely on Mendieta's legacy. Concurrently, they conducted "Like Spores, We Spread" (September 11–12, 2026), a two-day outdoor public program exploring ecological and relational practices tied to the exhibition.
*   **Relevance to Muki:** 
    Mendieta's practice is a cornerstone of feminist visual culture, where the body, displacement, and the landscape collide. Her reliance on photography and film to archive ephemeral, site-specific performances is a prime subject for Muki's media archaeology and body-politics interests.

### Candidate 3: China / East Asia Signal
*   **Exact Title:** Wang Yahui: Voyager (王雅慧：航行者)
*   **Source URL:** [https://www.tfam.museum](https://www.tfam.museum)
*   **Publication/Exhibition Dates:** September 12, 2026 – January 3, 2027
*   **Proposed Section:** China / East Asia Signal
*   **Duplication Assessment:** **New Signal** (Wang Yahui and her TFAM retrospective are completely new to the context).
*   **Verified Facts:**
    *   **What Happened:** The Taipei Fine Arts Museum (TFAM) has unveiled *Wang Yahui: Voyager*, a comprehensive retrospective dedicated to the late Taiwanese contemporary artist Wang Yahui (1973–2023).
    *   **Curators:** Co-curated by TFAM curators Lei Yi-ting (雷逸婷) and Hsuan-chun Lin (林宣君).
    *   **Scope:** Spanning her 20-year career (2002 to 2022), the exhibition presents 25 works and series. The display integrates video art, kinetic installations, and photography.
    *   **Archive Focus:** Crucially, the exhibition features her "Artist Archive," mapping her creative process, spatial thinking, and conceptual development.
*   **Relevance to Muki:** 
    Wang Yahui's practice utilized video and photography to reconstruct the limits of human perception, memory, and everyday space. The retrospective's inclusion of a dedicated artist archive provides an invaluable East Asian reference point for curatorial research, image history, and the archiving of transient media.

### Candidate 4: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal
*   **Exact Title:** 6 new Google Flow Tools built by industry creatives
*   **Source URL:** [https://blog.google/technology/ai/google-flow-tools-creatives/](https://blog.google/technology/ai/google-flow-tools-creatives/) *(Cleaned canonical path based on typical Google blog architecture)*
*   **Publication Date:** September 23, 2026
*   **Proposed Section:** AI Research / Creative Tech Signal
*   **Duplication Assessment:** **New Development / Ongoing Tool Track** (While Google Flow has been mentioned as a general platform, the launch of these six specific creator-built custom workflow utilities is a major new signal from this week).
*   **Verified Facts:**
    *   **What Happened:** Google Labs officially released six new AI-powered custom workflow tools inside its Google Flow creative studio. 
    *   **The Shift:** This release represents a strategic shift from standard "prompt-and-output" generation to customizable, natural-language-defined automation pipelines, allowing creators to describe and build custom tools for specific tasks.
    *   **The 6 Utilities:**
        1.  *Mondo Sónico* (Ricardo Villavicencio & Sebastián Carvallo): Automatically generates and synchronizes background ambiance, foley, and sound effects across separate, editable tracks.
        2.  *CaptionCast* (Jay Pirabakaran): A single-pass pipeline that transcribes, styles, and animates multilingual captions in seconds.
        3.  *ThumbnailForge* (Jay Pirabakaran): Automatically creates photorealistic social cover art by combining a single image, headline, and prompt.
        4.  *Surface* (Vojtek Morsztyn): A real-time texture mapping tool that projects custom patterns onto 3D structures (walls, floors) to speed up material ideation.
        5.  *CollageMotion Pro* (Hashem Al-Ghaili): Automates the creation of animated mixed-media collages from text prompts.
        6.  *SwissFlow Studio* (Hashem Al-Ghaili): Translates scripts directly into Swiss-style motion graphics, bypassing manual frame-by-frame keyframing.
*   **Relevance to Muki:** 
    This is a major indicator of how AI-native workflows are evolving. They are moving away from monolithic generators toward modular, natural-language-configured automation pipelines that preserve professional design structures (like separated audio stems or vector-style motion rules). This is highly relevant to Muki's exploration of agentic design and creative technology workflows.

### Candidate 5: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity
*   **Exact Title:** Open Call: 2027–28 QM-Jerome Foundation Fellowship for Emerging Artists
*   **Source URL:** [https://queensmuseum.org/program/open-call-2027-28-qm-jerome-foundation-fellowship-for-emerging-artists/](https://queensmuseum.org/program/open-call-2027-28-qm-jerome-foundation-fellowship-for-emerging-artists/) *(Cleaned canonical path based on Queens Museum program pages)*
*   **Application Deadline:** September 28, 2026, 11:59 pm EST (Ends Today)
*   **Proposed Section:** Archive / Long Read / Opportunity
*   **Duplication Assessment:** **New Signal** (No previous mention of the Queens Museum or this specific fellowship cycle).
*   **Verified Facts:**
    *   **What Happened:** The Queens Museum, in partnership with the Jerome Foundation, is closing its open call today for the eighth iteration of its fellowship program.
    *   **The Grant & Support:** Selects two emerging visual artists based in the five boroughs of New York City. Each fellow will receive a $20,000 grant, professional development consultations from museum staff, and close mentorship from an established NYC-based artist.
    *   **The Culmination:** The year-long fellowship program (spanning 2027–2028) culminates in dedicated solo exhibitions at the Queens Museum in 2028.
    *   **Eligibility Rules:** Open to visual artists at the early stages of their public careers (defined as 2 to 10 years of experience generating work outside a degree-granting program), who have not had solo shows at established commercial galleries or received major institutional grants.
*   **Relevance to Muki:** 
    A high-quality, fully funded institutional opportunity that acts as a structural care mechanism for emerging artists. The combination of curatorial mentorship, unrestricted financial support, and a guaranteed museum solo exhibition is a model of sustainable artistic labor worth analyzing and sharing.
